calls.reason: Reuters Institute found infrequent consumer use, while Microsoft reported substantial paid Copilot adoption and productivity benefits. This mixed evidence does not settle the undefined killer-app threshold.
The Princeton study found persistent reliability problems alongside small improvements. Neither establishes that those problems can never be solved.
Wu and colleagues and Lewis–Mitchell found substantial declines on controlled task variants. GSM1k shows exceptions, but does not negate the recurring tendency Marcus describes.
DeepMind's AlphaEvolve report supports improvements from search and verification. But the popularity clause is explicitly hedged and unmeasured here, so the full claim cannot be called.
The July 2024 WildHallucinations study documented factual hallucinations across 15 models and 118,785 generations. Adding retrieval reduced but did not eliminate them.
